key_insight: An uncertainty-aware framework translates predicted patient deterioration risks into ICU staffing plans while balancing staffing costs against severe shortages.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support ICU workforce planning by accounting for uncertain demand, rigid shifts, and hiring delays.
method: Converts probabilistic risk predictions into uncertainty-aware staffing demand signals without changing the prediction model.
Uses Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) to assess extreme shortage exposure.
Updates delay-constrained staffing decisions hourly through rolling-horizon scheduling.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on realistic MIMIC-IV trajectories showed a favorable cost–shortage trade-off versus deterministic and reactive baselines, with stress testing under calibration drift.
watch_item: The abstract reports trajectory-based evaluation, not prospective deployment or demonstrated improvements in patient outcomes.
paper_title: From Clinical Risk Prediction to Operational Decisions: An Uncertainty-Aware Framework for ICU Staffing
